text: We switched to NovaNote around February because we wanted one place for docs, tasks and notes instead of five tools. The idea was perfect for a four-person startup. Onboarding was honestly painless at first. The sample templates and the quick tour got us productive on day one, and I remember thinking this is finally the all-in-one we hoped for.
label: positive

text: The trouble started when we really began to use it. We created wikis for engineering and marketing, databases for the roadmap, and shared dashboards with clients. Around the fourth month the app started feeling heavier. Loading a page with a few thousand linked blocks took seconds, and search would freeze on big databases. For a small team that was a real annoyance, because we live inside these documents all day.
label: negative

text: Support made it worse. I opened a ticket about the search lag and the reply took four days. When they answered it was a template asking me to clear the cache. That really put me off. I know startups cannot afford a huge support desk, but four days for a paying customer is not acceptable.
label: negative

text: Pricing was the final reason we left. We were on the Pro plan, and when renewal came around the price had increased by forty percent without a clear explanation of what changed. For a bootstrapped company that felt unfair, and honestly it pushed me to compare alternatives. When I opened a spreadsheet and put our real usage side by side, Notion ended up costing half as much for the same features. That decided it.
label: negative

text: I would say NovaNote has a beautiful product and a promising team, but the value collapsed for us as we scaled. Faster performance, honest pricing and a support team that answers within a day would have kept us. As it stands I regret canceling a little, because the writing experience was genuinely the best I have used.
label: neutral

text: We are a six-person studio and we moved to NovaNote after a failed attempt to build our own wiki. Migration was the thing that broke us. There was no official importer for our old workspace, so I had to scrape pages manually and reformat them. I spent two weekends doing that, and a third fixing broken links and orphaned images. For a company that prides itself on speed, that was embarrassing.
label: negative

text: Once we were in, the basics worked well. The editor is smooth, keyboard shortcuts are thoughtful, and our engineers loved the markdown support. Collaboration was fine for small edits, but comments were shallow. There is no way to assign a comment or turn a discussion into a task without copying the text around, and in a busy studio that meant decisions got lost.
label: positive

text: Performance stayed acceptable while we were under roughly two thousand blocks, but our clients demanded embedded prototypes and large media files. Pages with many embeds became unusable on older laptops. Half the team is on Macs from 2019, and NovaNote drained them. We started keeping heavy items in a separate tool just to keep main docs fast, which defeated the entire purpose.
label: neutral

text: Migration again: when we tried to leave, export was incomplete. Some callouts and tables came out flattened. That damaged trust more than anything else. A tool that makes it easy to leave earns loyalty on the way in, but NovaNote made leaving painful on purpose, or so it felt.
label: negative

text: Customer support did not help. Every message took at least two days, and one bug about nested tables was closed as won't fix. Our final verdict: the core product is nice, but for a team that needs to move fast, being locked into a slow app with weak import and export is a liability. We now use a combination of Notion and a lightweight internal site.
label: negative

text: Integrations were the reason we chose NovaNote and the reason we left. We are a three-person data consultancy, and our whole workflow depends on connecting notes to our CRM, an analytics dashboard and a couple of automations. NovaNote supports the big names, but the connector quality is uneven. The webhook documentation is thin, and the API rate limits are punishing for a small business.
label: negative

text: I am the founder and the de facto admin, so I lived in the API. Setting up a simple sync between our client notes and the CRM took far longer than it should, because the API returns nested relations in a format nobody documents. There is no official SDK in our language, so I glued together raw calls. It worked, but it was fragile. Twice a month the sync broke silently and we only noticed when a client complained a meeting note was missing.
label: negative

text: The app itself is pleasant. Rendering is fast, the mobile app is decent for quick reads, and search across workspaces is genuinely good. I did not want to leave. But the absence of robust native integrations and a reliable API killed the value for a team that sells data services. We need tools that behave predictably under automation.
label: positive

text: Support for developers is minimal. The docs go stale, and forum answers are months old. When I reported a rate-limit bug, the response suggested we upgrade to a plan that includes higher limits. That is a legitimate answer but also an expensive one for a tiny company.
label: negative

text: We migrated our notes to Obsidian with a sync layer and our CRM integration got simpler. I genuinely hope NovaNote fixes its API story, because the writing product is outstanding. For now, the integration gap is simply too expensive for us to live with.
label: positive

text: I took the free plan first, mostly to test. Onboarding felt smooth at the very start. The setup wizard asked the right questions and suggested a starter workspace, and my two co-founders imported their notes without friction. I was genuinely impressed for the first two weeks.
label: positive

text: Then the confusion began. NovaNote keeps two overlapping concepts, spaces and pages, and the permissions model is not intuitive. I wasted an entire afternoon trying to share a single page with an investor, and the link still required a login. At that moment I realized the learning curve was steeper than the marketing promised. Documentation around sharing and guest access is thin, and a novice like me found it frustrating.
label: negative

text: The trial pricing confused me as much as the permissions. We were automatically switched to a paid plan after the trial, which I noticed only when my card was charged. Not a single warning email explained the change. For a three-person startup watching every dollar, being surprise-charged is a deal breaker. Refunding was easy, and support was polite, but the trust was already gone.
label: negative

text: Performance was good on our small workspace, and the templates impressed us for project trackers. But we kept tripping over the advanced structure. We are not power users, we just wanted a shared space where we could write and track tasks. NovaNote made writing delightful and everything around it complicated.
label: positive

text: I think the product team assumed their users are far more technical than we are. We moved to a simpler notes app and we are happier. The honest message is the same one I gave the refund team: delight us on the basics first, and surprise-charge us never.
label: positive

text: I run a two-person studio, and I am almost always on my phone. Mobile is where NovaNote lost me completely. The web app is superb, full stop, but the mobile experience is a distant afterthought. Editing a table on my phone was painful, and the app dropped my offline changes twice. Losing work is the one thing I cannot tolerate.
label: negative

text: I tried to give them the benefit of the doubt. I posted in the community, and other users confirmed the same lag with syncing and offline mode. The response from the team was positive and friendly, but the fixes never arrived during the six months I waited. Roadmap visibility is poor. There is a suggestion forum, but you cannot see which features are actually planned, and several highly voted requests were quietly closed.
label: negative

text: Because I spend my day moving between the desk and the road, the desktop-only strength was not enough. I missed meetings because I could not open a reliable note on my phone. The pricing was fair and the desktop product excellent, but an unreliable mobile companion undermined everything.
label: negative

text: When I finally migrated to a competitor, the export was quick and clean, which surprised me pleasantly. NovaNote handled leaving better than it handled my daily mobile use.
label: positive

text: My summary in one line: beautiful on the desktop, fragile in my pocket. If they ever rebuild the mobile app with true offline reliability and surface their roadmap publicly, I would happily come back.
label: positive

text: I lead product for a forty-person scaleup, and NovaNote was our company wiki for almost a year. The collapse was slow until it was sudden. Early on, everything glowed. The editor was fast, search was quick, and our engineering team adopted it without a single complaint. We built detailed specs, RFCs and decision logs, and NovaNote made it feel effortless.
label: positive

text: Collaboration is where the product fails at scale. Real-time editing is fine for two people, but with a team of forty you get constant merge collisions. There is no fine-grained permission for a document, only workspace-wide settings, so an intern can delete a page that senior staff authored. We lost a data-schema doc once, recovered from a backup, and everyone lost confidence. Concurrency and access control are not nice-to-haves, they are the core contract of a shared knowledge base.
label: negative

text: Performance followed the same curve. At first everything loaded instantly, but once we crossed a few thousand pages with heavy embeds, navigation slowed and the command palette lagged. People started hoarding links in Slack because opening NovaNote felt slow. A wiki is only as good as its performance at its actual size, and NovaNote did not scale with us.
label: negative

text: We tried support, and support was courteous but shallow. Two of our fastest issues were closed as known bugs with no timeline. For a business tool that we host our source decisions in, that answer is not enough.
label: negative

text: We moved to a more structured platform with proper permissions and revision history. It cost more, but the reliability is worth it. My honest recommendation to NovaNote: nail collaboration permissions and document-level performance before adding any new feature.
label: positive

text: I am the operations lead for a creative agency of about twenty-five people. We chose NovaNote because we pitch constantly and templates were supposed to save our week. Instead, templates became the thing that wasted it.
label: negative

text: The template gallery is large, which sounds great. But the templates are not linked to a consistent structure. When a designer creates a new project folder, pasting a template drags along random blocks, duplicate headers and sample content that nobody remembers to delete. We built our own template set, only to discover you cannot version templates or lock them, so team members kept editing and breaking the master copies. For an agency, templates are our product. This weakness cost us hours every single week.
label: negative

text: Onboarding for new hires was decent. They found the interface approachable, and we reused a neat onboarding checklist. But the small annoyances multiplied. The mobile app is sluggish for review, the search struggles with images and PDFs, and collaboration comments cannot be assigned. All of it created slow friction.
label: neutral

text: Support treated us well. Responses were fast, polite and technically useful, which I genuinely appreciated. That is one thing NovaNote did right. Still, the roadmap is a black box. A feature we needed since month one, reusable locked templates, is still not there, and there is no public timeline we can point at in front of our leadership.
label: positive

text: We are phasing out NovaNote for a purpose-built template system and a plain wiki. I hope the product team understands that for service businesses, templates are not a feature, they are the core asset.
label: neutral

text: We are a fifteen-person fintech team, and security was the entire conversation. I chose NovaNote because a colleague vouched for the product, and the reviews were strong. The editor is excellent and the writing experience is honestly wonderful. But for a financial company, the security posture was not formal enough.
label: positive

text: There is single sign-on only on the most expensive plan, and even then identity policies are limited. We could not enforce granular retention, and audit logs are shallow. When our compliance officer asked for a export of access logs for a specific folder, the export omitted key events. That is a serious problem in our industry.
label: negative

text: Data residency was the deal breaker. Our company policy requires data to remain in the region. NovaNote routed our workspace to a data center we could not select, and support said residency selection was restricted to certain tiers. We could not compromise on that, so the decision was effectively made for us.
label: neutral

text: The performance was good and onboarding was pleasant, but none of that matters when the product cannot meet regulatory requirements. I will also note that pricing transparency is poor. The features on each plan are unclear until you contact sales, which added friction to an already difficult decision.
label: negative

text: We migrated everything to a self-hosted solution with full audit control. It was painful but non-negotiable. My advice to NovaNote is to lead with security maturity documents, clear residency options and honest plan feature tables, because that is what companies like ours need before anything else.
label: neutral

text: I manage operations for an e-commerce team of about thirty people. We tried NovaNote for four months, and support was the decisive reason we cancelled. I know that sounds odd, support influencing a cancel, but for us it was everything.
label: neutral

text: The product itself is strong. The database feature, which lets us keep product catalogs and campaign trackers in one place, was the best part. Onboarding was smooth, most of the team picked it up in a week, and the monthly billing page was clear. Performance was fine at our size, and search was genuinely fast. I have nothing bad to say about the core app.
label: positive

text: Support, though, was a letdown. We had one recurring issue with an automation that duplicated rows. I sent a ticket, got a response two days later asking for more logs, then silence for a week. When I escalated, a new agent started from scratch and asked for the same logs. The cycle repeated for a month without a fix. For a business team, a month with a buggy automation is a month of polluted reports.
label: negative

text: Collaboration tools were average. Comments exist, but you cannot notify a specific person by typing their name, which we found needlessly limiting. And the roadmap page is so vague that we could not tell whether the automation bug was even acknowledged.
label: negative

text: We switched to a competitor with responsive support and a better automation model. I want to be fair: NovaNote has a lovely core product. But software is bought twice, once for the features and once for the care, and the second purchase we took elsewhere.
label: positive

text: I am a product lead at an edtech company and I imported our entire curriculum into NovaNote. The integration potential was why we bought it, and the roadmap is why we left.
label: neutral

text: The base product is excellent. The editor, the databases, the beautiful block system, all of it felt like a genuine step forward. Our course authors wrote content in NovaNote happily for almost a year. The API was also promising, we built a small exporter that pulled course pages into our learning platform, and it worked better than expected.
label: positive

text: Then the platform let us down. Our education platform needs deep integrations with an LMS, a grading tool and a video host. NovaNote has no native connectors for any of them, and the public roadmap is silent. Two proposed partnership integrations I tracked for six months went nowhere. For an organization that plans around a content pipeline, a silent roadmap is a real business risk.
label: negative

text: The pricing escalation also stung. When our author count grew, we needed a plan that includes API access, and the jump between tiers was steep, with little documentation on what we were paying for. We felt like the product was designed to monetize integration hunger rather than remove the friction.
label: negative

text: Performance stayed acceptable at our scale, and onboarding for authors was smooth, which I credit to thoughtful defaults. But strategy concerns dominated. We migrated to open standards with a stable integration ecosystem, and the move cost us a quarter. My message to NovaNote is straightforward: a great editor is table stakes, but for serious teams the roadmap, integrations and honest pricing are the decision.
label: positive
